text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed firmer in thin volume with many big players away due to public holidays across Europe and the absence of leading players in New York on account of this week's sugar dinner. August ended 10 cents higher at $318.40 per tonne, while October added 20 cents to close at $308 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed tightly mixed in dull trading. The July contract closed off 1 cent at 10.96 cents/lb after trading from 11.01 to 10.94 cents/lb. The outer contracts settled 1 cent higher to 3 cents lower. There was no fresh news to influence trading.

ARGENTINA - Sugar production in Argentina in 1997/98 (June/May) is forecast to reach 1.575 million tonnes, raw value, up from 1.394 million tonnes produced the previous year, but down from 1.611 million tonnes produced in 1995/96. This means that the country will have to import no sugar in 1997/98.

CANADA - Canada imported 494,448 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in October/February 1996/97, 5.9 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1995/96. Total imports in crop year 1995/96 (October/September) reached 1.160 million tonnes, up from 1.013 million tonnes imported the previous year. The main supplier of raw sugar in October/February 1996/97 was Australia with 399,967 tonnes vs 361,659 tonnes the same period in 1995/96. White sugar imports from the US dropped sharply in October/February 1996/97 to 2,079 tonnes, down from 18,336 tonnes the same period in 1995/96. Sugar production in 1997/98 (October/December) is forecast to fall to 108,000 tonnes, raw value, down from 156,000 tonnes produced in 1996/97 and 163,000 tonnes produced in 1995/96.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports from third countries in March 1997 amounted to 93,684 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 596,854 tonnes against 641,666 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports from third countries in 1995/96 amounted to 1.298 million tonnes. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Mauritius with 271,983 tonnes against 332,907 tonnes, Guyana with 111,673 tonnes compared to 73,510 tonnes and Fiji with 79,900 tonnes, down from 85,180 tonnes. Sugar exports to third countries in March 1997 reached 42,061 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in 1996/97 up to 131,784 tonnes, down from 140,089 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports to third countries in 1995/96 reached 324,415 tonnes. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Israel with 60,820 tonnes whites against 50,717 tonnes, Norway with 19,131 tonnes compared with 21,306 tonnes and Hong Kong with 14,959 tonnes, up from 10,136 tonnes.

PORTUGAL - Portugal imported 10,443 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in January 1997, 36 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1996 reached 310,625 tonnes, roughly the same what was imported in 1995. The main suppliers of raw sugar in January 1997 were Mauritius (6,661 vs 0 tonnes), Swaziland (2,000 vs 14,679 tonnes) and Fiji (1,755 vs 0 tonnes).

UKRAINE - The Ukraine exported 250,109 tonnes of white sugar in January/March 1997. The main country of destination was Russia with 159,600 tonnes. Smaller quantities went to Azerbaidjan (11,599 tonnes), Belarus (13,300 tonnes) and Turkmenistan (14,001 tonnes). TENDERS

Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) has issued a buying tender for 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws. June 17 is the final date for price offers and the two amounts should be shipped between July 15 and August 15.
